claims.quote: I find this only exacerbates my issue with them.

verdicts.trueWording: judges felt that the actual description of dungeons was their 'domain'
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched (dmdavid.com tag page renders the full 2016-11-21 post, bylined David Hartlage). Under heading 'Tegel Manor and minimal descriptions': introduced as 'In Dragon magazine issue 27, Bob Bledsaw wrote'. Every limb holds (Hartlage; Bledsaw; Dragon 27; judges' own domain). Bledsaw's sentence continues that all judges wanted was a skeletal framework.

verdicts.trueWording: A lot of this involves de-bullet pointing the text.
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Opening paragraph, dated March 23 2023: the rewrite is of 'Behind Closed Doors', shown to be his own by 'I'm a better writer than I was three years ago' and 'even my bullet-points'. 'Largely' tracks the page's 'a lot of this'. Only nuance: the page says bullets -> prose, never that the text had been prose before ('back into').

verdicts.trueWording: I find this only exacerbates my issue with them.
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Same opening paragraph; the preceding sentence is that even his bullet-points are more prose-based than a lot of other examples he has seen. Both limbs (more prose-based than most; worsens rather than eases the objection) are on the page.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the prose keys a room 'from a single dominant smell or object outward'
verdicts.trueWording: The old bricks of the kitchen are stained black with soot.
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched; the quoted smell line is verbatim in the room 4 Kitchen prose version, and the prose is present tense throughout. But it is the SECOND sentence: room 4 opens on the soot-stained bricks. The page never states a method, and the demonstrated openings are not uniform - rooms 10 and 14 open on a bare adjective ('Austere.', 'Pristine, kept in readiness'), room 12 on an abstraction, while rooms 8 and 13 do open on a smell. The lead-from-a-dominant-sensory-anchor rule is the researcher's inference, not the page's claim.

verdicts.trueWording: I often just close my eyes and imagine being there
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched (post dated September 14 2021), under 'Structures' > 'Mental Dig/Exploration'. Supported, with two framings the claim flattens: the page conditions it on already having 'a good sense of the vibe and tone of a physical space', says 'often', and offers it as one of five interchangeable structures (Mental Dig, Map First, Pearl, Resonance & Conflict, Timeline) to 'move between as you see fit'.

verdicts.trueWording: finding those touchstones which communicate the tone
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Same 'Mental Dig/Exploration' paragraph, which lists three uses: fine-tuning the vibe/tone, finding those touchstones, and finding out what else is there. The walk-through limb is the same paragraph's 'moving from room to room, the contents of physical space begin to suggest themselves to me'.

verdicts.trueWording: The introduction is highly evocative, reading almost like the weird fiction
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Section 'SAMPLE DUNGEON', second sentence; the page continues 'that Holmes was a fan of'. One attribution note: the post is bylined 'Zenopus Archives', not 'Zach Howard' - the identification is corroborated on the Delta page fetched for this same chunk, which credits 'Zach Howard (Zenopus)'.

verdicts.trueWording: should read the background material above to the assembled players
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Quoted Holmes manuscript text: 'The Dungeon Master should read the background material above to the assembled players and then let them decide how they will proceed.' 'Aloud' is entailed by 'read ... to the assembled players'. The 1977 attribution survives: the post names only two changes to the introduction in the published rulebook (the second sentence moved to the paragraph's end; 'assistants' -> 'men-at-arms'), neither touching this instruction.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'predating boxed text' - the page never mentions boxed text at all
verdicts.trueWording: this background material is meant to be read to the players
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched; the quotation is verbatim in Howard's commentary on the Portown paragraph ('- this background material is meant to be read to the players, as indicated below'), and the read-to-the-players limb is fully supported. The chronological limb is absent: the words 'boxed text' do not occur anywhere on the page (checked against the full raw text, comments included), so the page cannot support the claim that this practice predates boxed text.

verdicts.trueWording: Here we get a thumbnail sketch of a campaign setting
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Commentary immediately below the quoted Holmes paragraph, which is one paragraph covering caravan routes from the south (trade), merchant ships on pirate-infested waters, and humans and non-humans from all over the globe (inhabitants). Every limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: And hey, there's boxed text for the first time!
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Closing line of the section headed '1982 - Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth Publication', and corroborated later in the same post: the 1983-85 adventures use boxed text 'as introduced in the 1982 Tsojcanth dungeon areas'. 'First' is first within Delta's declared sample - adventures authored by Gygax at two-year intervals across 1974-1985.

verdicts.trueWording: only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Section '1974 - Castle Greyhawk Notes'; the sentence continues 'noting monster type, number range, and treasure (and absolutely nothing else)'. Two hedges the claim drops: the notes were never published (known from a photo taken at a Gen Con 2007 event), and Delta records debate over whether the encounter text is original, with the map dated 'could be 1972-1974 or so'. He also notes the key is sparser still - one number often covers several rooms and about three-quarters are unkeyed.

verdicts.trueWording: the paragraphs tend to lead with those sense-descriptions
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Section '1978 - Steading of the Hill Giant Chief'; the sentence continues that monster identification and hit points possibly occur deeper in the block, which is the point of the observation. Both limbs (the 1978 module; paragraphs leading with sense-descriptions) hold.

verdicts.trueWording: almost 500 words total for the one area
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. Section '1980 - Expedition to the Barrier Peaks', on area 7, the 'Ship Commander's Quarters'. The no-monsters limb is doubly supported: the area is offered as an example of deeply detailed areas 'even without any monsters or traps at all', and its sub-areas a-d are parenthesised as having no monsters or unnatural contents. Delta's word count covers area 7 with those sub-areas, matching the claim's 'an area'.

verdicts.trueWording: 2 full pages of text to be read verbatim
verdicts.note: Live raw page fetched. In the final section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil', where Delta brings in 1985's Isle of the Ape: an introductory boxed-speech by Tenser running two full pages to be read verbatim, parenthesised as 'some 1,600 words!'. Every limb (opens with; boxed; Tenser; ~1,600 words; read verbatim) holds.
